title: We are patchwork
hook: we are all patchwork, and each piece plays its own game (Essays 2.1)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was laughing and weeping: Montaigne chose the laugh, because our trouble is less malice than folly. Your line was laugh, don't weep.

Calm in the meeting, furious in the parking lot. Patient with a stranger's toddler, short with your own mother. Generous on Monday, petty by Thursday. So which one is the real you? Montaigne takes up that question in the essay that opens the second book of the Essays, and his answer is uncomfortable and oddly freeing. It's all of them. And none of them stays in charge for long.
screen: `CALM HERE, FURIOUS THERE.` → `WHICH ONE IS REAL?` → `ALL OF THEM.`

segments.voice: First, the puzzle. In Of the Inconstancy of Our Actions, Montaigne says that people who study human behavior find nothing harder than fitting our actions together into one steady picture. We contradict ourselves so often that it's easier to believe we're changeable than consistent. So, he says, it's unfair to judge a person by a single act. Second, the image. We are all patchwork, he writes, so shapeless and mixed in our making that each piece, each moment, plays its own game. Then the line that stings: there's as much difference between us and ourselves as between us and other people. Third, the confession. He doesn't exempt himself. He turns his soul one way and shows one face, he says, then turns it and shows another. He finds in himself bashful and bold, talkative and silent, truthful and lying, generous and stingy, depending on which side he looks from. Fourth, the week's patches. Imagination, which can make us ill or well. Custom, which makes anything seem normal. A head well made, not full. Who are the barbarians? The back shop. Laugh, don't weep. Montaigne never sews these into one system, and he doesn't try. Each essay is a patch. This one is a mercy, in two directions: toward the person who snapped at you, and toward the you who snapped back.
screen: `HARD TO BE CONSISTENT.` · `EACH PIECE PLAYS ITS OWN GAME.` · `BOLD AND BASHFUL, BOTH.` · `A WEEK OF PATCHES.` · then, large: `PATCHWORK.`

segments.voice: Bring back one recent moment when you were at your best, steady, kind and clear, and another when you were somebody else, rushed, sharp, small. Don't choose which one is real; set them side by side like two squares of cloth. Both are yours, so breathe with both of them there.
We are patchwork. Montaigne's picture of a person: made of pieces, each moment playing its own game, as different from ourselves as from others. Today's word.
Your line: patchwork. Nobody is only their worst piece, or only their best. I'll be here tomorrow.
